Can confirm this on Hyprland with Godot 4.5. Both the main editor and floating popup windows open using native Wayland, not through XWayland. It isn't a deal breaker but still I'd love to see this issue fixed in the next release.
Floating windows opened by another floating window are scaled properly though. For example, visually selecting a path for a new script or shader.

Just wanted to mention that I can also confirm seeing this (using "Prefer Wayland" in Godot). It's very frustrating because Waybar (the bar on top) will then cover the floating/pop-up windows that are maximizing vertically. And no amount of things I've tried has been able to solve this issue on Hyprland.

> And no amount of things I've tried has been able to solve this issue on Hyprland.

You can actually fix this by setting the "Single Window Mode" setting on in the Editor Settings > Interface > Editor. This makes Godot "emulate" pop-up windows in the main window like it was previously implemented with Wayland in 4.4

> > And no amount of things I've tried has been able to solve this issue on Hyprland.
> 
> You can actually fix this by setting the "Single Window Mode" setting on in the Editor Settings > Interface > Editor. This makes Godot "emulate" pop-up windows in the main window like it was previously implemented with Wayland in 4.4

I actually gave this a shot. It does solve the problem with Waybar being overtop of the floating windows, which is better. I can definitely use this until a more proper fix is in place!

However, I wouldn't say this is a "fix", per se. The original problem is definitely still a massive problem. But definitely a temporary workaround that I'll use!

Thanks for letting me know about it! :)

Hi, sorry, this issue slipped under my radar.

From a quick look I'm not entirely sure what we're doing wrong. We're parenting all dialogs to the main window which should (and seems to?) mark the window as a dialog but that doesn't seem enough for some reason. If I'm reading correctly the linked issue it looks like the window is always marked as maximized, for CSD reasons.

Perhaps implementing the new `xdg-dialog-v1` protocol could help? It doesn't look like niri implements it though and I don't think that would fix the CSD thing.

I'm really, really not sure what's the expected behavior that we should implement to have properly sized dialogs on those two compositors.

This thread seems to have a lot of smart people who have been discussing the issue quite intensely, and I've tried getting a bunch of smart Wayland folks involved: https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/9171

95% of it is over my head, but at the core it seems that:

https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/420 - This is a problem with the Wayland spec. This merge request attempts to fix it. Gnome does not intend to fix it.

Then there's this of text that gave me an explanation of what is going on:

> There is this thing called client side decorations (CSD), which means that the window itself (e.g. the file manager or Godot or Firefox) draws some window controls like for example an X for closing the window or a - to minimize it. This is opposed to server side decorations (SSD) where the compositor (like Hyprland or KDE or Gnome) would draw these icons. So the difference is about who is drawing these icons (or even shadows and stuff like that). The advantage of the latter is a "unified look", and the advantage of the former is that it can be nicely integrated with the rest of the window. (E.g. in a browser the X for closing the window could go on the same height as the tab list, and can adapt to the browser theme.)

> Now of course the compositor and the window should agree on whether they are using CSD or SSD. And in particular for Hyprland, which is a tiling compositor, we want to use SSD. (Because we close our windows with some shortcut, not by clicking any X. We don't want that the windows draws any X or any shadows.)

> Now the problem that people were facing at some point is that there is no nice way to tell windows that they should stop drawing their CSD, or at least that not all windows adhere to that (in particular GTK windows).

> Now it turned out that @vaxerski found a sneaky hack: If you just tell the windows they are maximized (even though they are not), then suddenly they won't draw any shadows etc., because they think they are fullscreen anyway! So from now on Hyprland will just tell EVERY window that it's maximized (even though it's not). And that's what Hyprland still does.

> Now, unfortunately, this breaks some things.

The author of Hyprland came back with this:

> The problem is we can't just "let the apps draw CSD". The big problem is about the non-window CSD, like shadows. The renderer will not handle those, and it will be even worse than it is right now.

> The reason why KDE or Gnome get away is that they do draw those, but Hyprland literally can't or it becomes a detriment to UX (shadows overlap other tiled windows). This is also what happens on other tiling wayland compositors as far as I can tell.

> What you can do (and what we used to do in the past) was cut out the shadows in the renderer via some uv math, but the math got so out of hand with 200 different things needing to adjust it that I eventually dropped it because it was actively causing problems.

> The actual fix is to either get the MR (https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/420) we proposed down, or just... remember size when maximized.

I don't know if that explains the current situation enough so that you understand it (I certainly don't), but hopefully it can be a starting point to see if there's anything the Godot team can do to overcome it for Hyprland/Niri/other Wayland-based window managers (which seem like they are growing in popularity pretty fast).

And maybe someone from the Godot team can weigh in or throw some insight or support for: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/420

Edit: sorry, to be clear, by protocol dump I mean the usual incantation we use for godot: `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 gimp 2>&1 | tee wl-gimp.log`

Here it is: [wl-gimp.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22874159/wl-gimp.log)

Behavior was basically only launching GIMP, then issuing two [`killactive`](https://wiki.hypr.land/Configuring/Dispatchers/#list-of-dispatchers) dispatches through a keybind, which close the welcome dialog and then the main app. No mouse movement done at all.

Also if useful, did the same for Godot: [wl-godot.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22874172/wl-godot.log). Also only opened a testing project, issued a `killactive` dispatch (which opens the "save work before closing" dialog), then pressed Enter to select Save & Quit.
